# Laravel TDD

Curated by Skill Harbor: test-driven development for Laravel applications, so Muse writes tests first and features second. Covers the full red-green-refactor cycle: PHPUnit configuration for testing (in-memory SQLite, array cache, mail and queue fakes), base TestCase helpers (actingAsUser, actingAsAdmin), model factories with states and sequences (UserFactory with admin and unverified states, relationships, make versus create), model tests (hidden attributes, scopes, relationships), feature and HTTP tests (guest redirects, validation errors, authorization boundaries like users-can-only-modify-their-own), JSON API tests (paginated lists, assertJsonStructure, 401 for unauthenticated), Sanctum token auth testing (register, login, wrong password, bearer token), mocking with Laravel fakes (Http::fake with sequences, Mail::fake, Notification::fake, Queue::fake, Storage::fake, Event::fake), Artisan command tests, authorization tests (policies, gates, super-admin), Pest-style feature tests, and coverage setup with goals per component (models 95%+, services 90%+, overall 80%+). Includes a quick-reference table of every assertion helper and DO/DON'T testing best practices (factories over manual create, one logical assertion per test, never test framework internals, never couple tests). Use when writing Laravel tests with PHPUnit or Pest, or driving a Laravel feature test-first. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest...
